moldova-vs-kazakhstan.teamNews:
Team News
Moldova have no players suspended for this match, but Iurie Iovu, Vadim Rata and Oleg Reabciuk are one booking away from missing the team's next game.
Petru Popescu has scored twice in eight appearances for his country and is once again expected to feature in the final third of the field on Friday.
There should also be a start in midfield for Nichita Motpan.
As for Kazakhstan, Sergey Malyy is suspended for Friday's match following his red card in the team's last fixture in the competition.
Ramazan Karimov and Galymzhan Kenzhebek are set to feature in the final third of the field on Friday, while Georgi Zhukov will be a notable starter in a deeper area for the visitors.
Moldova possible starting lineup:
Celeadnic; Reabciuk, Baboglo, Iovu, Dumbravanu; Motpan, Perciun, Cojocari, Fratea; Popescu, Clescenco

Pokatilov; Alip, Kassym, Zhagorov, Tapalov; Ashirbek, Kuat, Zhukov, Amir; Kenzhebek, Karimov
We say: Moldova 1-1 Kazakhstan
Both teams are searching for valuable wins in Group C3, but the pair might have to settle for a share of the spoils in this Nations League fixture.

Team News
© Imago / Guillermo Martinez
Bulgaria must be careful to avoid needless yellow cards on Friday given eight players are at risk of picking up a suspension, though they know they will be able to welcome back goalkeeper Dimitar Mitov and winger Lukas Petkov.
Mitov is likely to be stationed behind a back four featuring centre-backs Stefan Velkov and Emil Tsenov, while Andrian Kraev and Ilia Gruev could start in a double pivot.
Petkov is set to start on the right side of attack, with Kristiyan Balov on the left flank and Atanas Iliev through the middle.
Iceland could position Andri Gudjohnsen in an advanced role behind striker Orri Oskarsson, with the pair likely to be supported by midfielders Gylfi Sigurdsson and Isak Bergmann Johannesson.
Central defenders Brynjar Ingi Bjarnason and Hordur Magnusson are candidates to start in the heart of a back four.
Bulgaria possible starting lineup:
Mitov; Stoyanov, Velkov, Tsenov, Petrov; Kraev, Gruev; Petkov, Rusev, Balov; Iliev
Iceland possible starting lineup:
Valdimarsson; Palsson, Bjarnason, Magnusson, Gretarsson; Sigurdsson, Johannesson; Haraldsson, Gudjohnsen, Anderson; Oskarsson
We say: Bulgaria 0-2 Iceland
Though home advantage has often been crucial for many teams, Bulgaria have struggled for consistency when playing as hosts.
Iceland have also performed well on their travels in the Nations League, and they should be confident that they can take three points on Friday.

netherlands-vs-greece.teamNews:
Team News
© Iconsport / DeFodi Images
The hosts must negotiate their final pair of group games without Ryan Gravenberch, Kenneth Taylor, 
Brian Brobbey and Van Dijk
, all of whom have withdrawn due to injury.
Brentford's Sepp van den Berg has been drafted in as cover for Oranje's vastly experienced skipper, who received his 100th international cap last month.
Juventus midfielder Teun Koopmeiners partnered Van Dijk against Serbia, but the more conventional North London duo of Jan Paul van Hecke and Jurrien Timber are likely to play on Friday night.
Mexx Meerdink impressed in Xavi's first camp, yet Donyell Malen will expect to start after returning to the squad, having scored 14 goals in 12 Roma appearances this season.
Another Serie A star, Douvikas recently netted a Champions League hat-trick; however, he faces a fight to displace Vangelis Pavlidis or Fotis Ioannidis in the visitors' front line.
In fact, Jovanovic has plenty of attacking options to choose from, including Konstantinos Karetsas and Premier League pair Christos Tzolis and Charalampos Kostoulas.
After picking up their second booking of the campaign against Germany, both Christos Zafeiris and Manolis Saliakas must serve a one-match ban; the latter's absence offers a chance for Lazaros Rota or Georgios Vagiannidis to start at right-back.
Netherlands possible starting lineup:
Verbruggen; Dumfries, J. Timber, Van Hecke, Van de Ven; Q. Timber, De Jong, Veerman; Summerville, Malen, Gakpo
Greece possible starting lineup:
Tzolakis; Vagiannidis, Mavropanos, Koulierakis, Tsimikas; Masouras, Kourbelis, Androutsos, Tzolis; Ionannidis, Pavlidis
We say: Netherlands 3-2 Greece
As the Netherlands can be caught out at the back - and their visitors have a bright crop of attacking talent - there should be more goals, after the teams' entertaining contest last month.
Though Greece are a rising force, their unbeaten streak could come to an end, as Xavi can welcome back Malen and Frenkie de Jong - even if his injured captain will be missed.

scotland-vs-n-macedonia.teamNews:
Team News
© Iconsport / PA Images
Scotland are boosted by the return of Scott McTominay, who did not feature in the first four Nations League matches due to undergoing heart surgery. 
The midfielder is expected to return straight into the starting 11, providing attacking support for Oli McBurnie, with John McGinn, Lewis Ferguson and Billy Gilmour featuring in midfield. 
At the back, Aaron Hickey could start on the right of a back-three, alongside Jack Hendry and Luis Binks, while Ben Gannon-Doak and Andy Robertson provide width from wing-back.
As for North Macedonia, captain Enis Bardhi should start in attacking midfield, with Ljupche Doriev and Dimitar Mitrovski providing support from the wings for striker Elmin Rastoder.
Further back, Eljif Elmas and Jani Atanasov should start at the base of midfield, with Visar Misliu and Anes Meljichi starting in central defence.
Scotland possible starting lineup:
Gunn; Hickey, Hendry, Binks; Doak, McGinn, Ferguson, Gilmour, Robertson; McTominay; McBurnie
North Macedonia possible starting lineup:
Dimitrievski; Ilievski, Meljichi, Misliu, Alioski; Elmas, Atanasov, Mitrovski, Bardhi, Doriev; Rastoder
We say: Scotland 2-0 North Macedonia
Scotland may be enduring a difficult run, but they demonstrated their superiority over the struggling North Macedonia in the reverse fixture and should secure another comfortable win on Friday.

Team News
© Imago / Maximilian Koch
Serbia will be without the services of two players through suspension, with Sasa Lukic and Nemanja Maksimovic ruled out of the contest with Germany.
Aleksandar Mitrovic is in line to win his 107th cap for his country, and the 32-year-old could be joined in the final third of the field by Mihajlo Cvetkovic, who has one goal in five matches for Serbia.
There is also set to be a spot in the middle of the midfield for Sergej Milinkovic-Savic.
Germany, meanwhile, have three players one booking away from a suspension, with Philipp Treu, Malick Thiaw and Yann Bisseck all in danger of missing the team's final fixture in the group stage of the 2026-27 Nations League.
Kai Havertz
 has scored 25 times for Germany and is once again expected to feature through the middle, while Florian Wirtz could also be in line for a starting role on Friday.
Said El Mala and Lennart Karl could be involved from the first whistle, while Marc-Andre ter Stegen has been confirmed as Germany's number one goalkeeper.
Serbia possible starting lineup:
V Milinkovic-Savic; Nedeljkovic, Gudelj, Babic, Erakovic, Sukacev; Samardzic, S Milinkovic-Savic, Zivkovic; Cvetkovic, Mitrovic
Germany possible starting lineup:
Ter Stegen; Treu, Tah, Schlotterbeck, Brown; Nmecha, Kimmich; El Mala, Wirtz, Karl; Havertz
We say: Serbia 1-2 Germany
Germany have been far from convincing in this Nations League tournament, but Serbia have also struggled, and we are backing Klopp's side to secure a valuable three points on Friday.

Team News
© Iconsport / Dominika Kortvelyesiova
Slovakia will be lighter in midfield than ideal without 
Stanislav Lobotka
 (ankle) and the versatile Tomas Suslov (hamstring), though Peter Pokorny could be joined by Tomas Rigo and Ondrej Duda in the centre of the park.
Further forward, Middlesbrough's David Strelec may lead the attack, supported from out wide by Tomas Bobcek and Lukas Haraslin.
As for Faroe Islands, they are missing Mjallby left wing-back Martin Agnarsson, who is suspended after being sent off against Kazakhstan.
Filling the gaps this week, Klakstein could opt for Samuel Johansen Chukwudi on the left flank, with Joannes Kalso Danielsen on the right.
Elsewhere, Petur Knudsen should be on hand to start up top, supplied by Aki Samuelsen and Hanus Sorensen.
Slovakia possible starting lineup:
Greif; Mesik, Skriniar, Obert, Hancko; Rigo, Pokorny, Duda; Bobcek, Strelec, Haraslin
Faroe Islands possible starting lineup:
Lamhauge; Faero, Vatnhamar, Edmundsson; Danielsen, Turi, Bjartalid, Chukwudi; Samuelsen, Knudsen, Sorensen
We say: Slovakia 2-1 Faroe Islands
Slovakia are the favourites owing to the superior quality in their squad, and their 81-better FIFA ranking, though they are unlikely to pull off a second consecutive thrashing.
Faroe Islands are the only nation that have caused the Falcons to drop points in Group C3, so expect to see another close-fought contest between two unbeaten sides.
